mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate, as measured by the FEDFUNDS series, indicates an easing monetary policy that reduces the discount rate for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS declines over the prior month, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 4.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE > 4.5, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both residential investment (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate a weakening housing market that reduces consumer wealth and spending, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where both RSAFS and HOUST decline, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO below 100), supply chain constraints and reduced manufacturing output lead to higher inflation expectations, triggering a sell-off in equities and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where INDPRO < 100, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential investment (RSAFS) indicates strong household demand that supports corporate revenue growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where RSAFS increases, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly year-over-year increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 3.5% signals accelerating inflation that prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where CPIAUCSL YoY change > 3.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in employment growth (PAYEMS) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) indicate a severe labor market contraction that reduces consumer confidence and spending, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%), the cost of capital increases, reducing the present value of future equity cash flows and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.0, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.02.
